1971 expectations yet to be fulfilled
2013-03-22T00:15:19+06:00 | Staff Correspondent, Ctg
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/1971-expectations-yet-to-be-fulfilled

Discussants at a roundtable, “42 Years of Independence: Evaluation of Expectation and Achievements in Present Context”, organised by The Daily Star at its Chittagong city office yesterday. Photo: Star

Most of the expectations from the country's Liberation War have not been fulfilled even after 42 years of independence, speakers said at a discussion yesterday.

They said the people hoped for economic freedom, education for all, rights of women and children, and above all a secular state and the rule of law.

Enamul Hoque Danu, freedom fighter and general secretary of Chittagong city unit Awami League, said, “We expected that people from all walks of life would get their rights. We also expected that the wealth of the country would not be centralised but distributed evenly throughout the country. This expectation is yet to be fulfilled."

Syed Ahsanul Alam, professor of Chittagong University, said the people joined the 1971 war for being discriminated against socially, culturally and economically. "Although we have achieved political freedom, we have failed to achieve economic freedom."

The roundtable, “42 years of Independence: Evaluation of Expectation and Achievements in Present Context”, was jointly organised by The Daily Star and Imperial Group at The Daily Star Conference Centre in Chittagong city.

Freedom fighter and general secretary of the Communist Party of Bangladesh, Chittagong Shah Alam, freedom fighter Dr Mahfuzur Rahman, Principal of Fulki Sahojpath Shila Momen, Advocate Mili Chowdhury, The Daily Star Chittagong Bureau Chief Raisul Haq Bahar, and journalist Uday Shankar Das were present on the occasion among others.
